findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update evaluates the org-wrapped model, so edits made while the org is disabled can leave the cache stale
findings.body: `update()` takes `original` from `getById()`, which returns the organization-aware wrapper. The wrapper's `isEnabled()` also returns false when the linked org, or the organization feature, is disabled. `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` therefore reports 'not a login IDP' for any org-linked IDP while its org is disabled, whatever its stored state. The updated model comes straight from the request and is not wrapped. Example: the org is disabled and an admin sets hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true or enabled=false on a previously listed IDP. Both `original` and `updated` test as non-login, so the method returns early and registers no invalidation. The cached id set still contains an IDP that the database query now excludes. Once the org is re-enabled, `getForLogin` returns the stale id set. The bean's added `isEnabled()` re-check only covers the enabled case, so a hidden or link-only IDP would show up on the login page until something else invalidates the entry. The comparison should use the stored (unwrapped) state of the original IDP, for example the cached delegate model.

findings.title: remove() now always queries the database for the IDP, even when it is cached
findings.body: `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now called unconditionally at the top of `remove()`. Before, it was only called when the alias key was already invalidated in the transaction. In the common case, where the alias entry is cached, this adds an extra DB round trip on every removal. The stored model is needed only for the login-invalidation check. It could be taken from the cached entry that is already looked up, and fetched from the delegate only when that entry is missing or invalidated.

findings.title: Cache search key includes organizationId even for REALM_ONLY mode, where it is ignored
findings.body: `searchKey` is always derived from `organizationId`. For `FetchMode.REALM_ONLY` the delegate ignores the organization id, so each distinct org id produces a separate but identical entry. Every new key also triggers the `invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and re-add path, which bumps the revision for that cache key. The search key should be normalized, for example to "" for REALM_ONLY, so the entry is shared.

findings.title: Cleanup registered with the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP's alias
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets an IDP literally named "alias", not the one just created (`idp-alias-N`). The same bug is on line 425, and the pattern is copied from the existing test. The 21 IDPs created by this test are never removed. Cleanup will either fail with a 404 or silently do nothing, depending on the cleanup implementation. The leftover IDPs can leak into other tests, because several tests assert exact IDP counts. The cleanup should use the actual alias variable.

findings.title: Test does not exercise creating or removing an IDP that is available for login
findings.body: The invalidation tests only create a non-login IDP (hideOnLogin) and remove a non-login IDP (a disabled one), and assert the caches survive. The new `create()` and `remove()` invalidation for IDPs that qualify for login is never tested. A regression there would go unnoticed. The test also only checks the size of the cached id sets, not what `getForLogin` actually returns. It does not cover the org-disabled scenario that the new `isEnabled()` re-check in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` exists for. Add cases that create and remove a login IDP and assert the cache is cleared, and cases that verify the returned content.
